records.gloss: And now, to you [is] this commandment, O priests.
pieces: And now, you priests, this command is for you.

L.1: And now, to you [is] this commandment, O priests.

R.1: Now, you priests, here is a warning for you.

decisions.choice: this commandment: the LORD's decree, the warning that follows
alternatives: the charge given to the priests
decisions.reason: The word usually means a command. Here it is the decree of verses 2-3, a warning that is also a command to give glory to the LORD's name. Verse 4 says that it was sent to preserve the LORD's covenant with Levi. |

decisions.choice: and now, O priests: the charge of 1:6-14 comes to its verdict
decisions.reason: The LORD has shown how the priests despise his name (1:6-14). Now he tells them what will follow if they do not change. |

decisions.choice: a warning (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "warning", the sense the word has here (m1). |

records.heading: A warning to the priests

records.source: אִם־לֹ֣א תִשְׁמְע֡וּ וְאִם־לֹא֩ תָשִׂ֨ימוּ עַל־לֵ֜ב לָתֵ֧ת כָּב֣וֹד לִשְׁמִ֗י אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וְשִׁלַּחְתִּ֤י בָכֶם֙ אֶת־הַמְּאֵרָ֔ה וְאָרוֹתִ֖י אֶת־בִּרְכֽוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם וְגַם֙ אָרוֹתִ֔יהָ כִּ֥י אֵינְכֶ֖ם שָׂמִ֥ים עַל־לֵֽב׃
records.gloss: If you do not listen, and if you do not lay [it] on heart to give glory to my name, says Yahweh of hosts, then I will send on you the curse, and I will curse your blessings; and indeed I have cursed it, because you are not laying [it] on heart.
pieces: If you will not listen, and if you will not resolve to give glory to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, \q I will send the curse on you \q and turn your blessings into curses. \q In fact, I have already cursed them, \q because you have not taken this to heart.

L.2: If you will not listen, and if you will not lay [it] to heart to give glory to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, \q then I will send the curse upon you, \q and I will curse your blessings; \q indeed, I have already cursed it, \q because you are not laying [it] to heart.

R.2: Listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and decide to give glory to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. If you do not, \q I will put a curse on you. \q I will turn your blessings into curses. \q In fact, I have already done this, \q because you have not taken it seriously.

decisions.choice: lay it to heart: take it seriously, resolve to act
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought and will. To lay something on the heart is to think about it and decide to act on it (Isaiah 42:25; 57:1). |

decisions.choice: your blessings: the blessings you pronounce, or the good things you receive
decisions.reason: The priests were to bless the people in the LORD's name (Numbers 6:23-27), and the LORD will turn their blessings into curses. "Blessings" can also mean the gifts and portions the priests received. Either way, what should bring good will bring harm.

decisions.choice: the curse: the curse of the covenant
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 28:15-20 warns that if Israel will not listen to the LORD, curses will come on all they do. The priests, who should teach the covenant, fall under its curse. |

decisions.choice: give glory to my name (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: "Glory" follows the Isaiah table at every level. Readable puts the command first and the threat after, to keep sentences short. |

records.source: הִנְנִ֨י גֹעֵ֤ר לָכֶם֙ אֶת־הַזֶּ֔רַע וְזֵרִ֤יתִי פֶ֨רֶשׁ֙ עַל־פְּנֵיכֶ֔ם פֶּ֖רֶשׁ חַגֵּיכֶ֑ם וְנָשָׂ֥א אֶתְכֶ֖ם אֵלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: Look, I [am] rebuking the seed for you, and I will spread dung on your faces, [the] dung of your festivals; and [one] will carry you to it.
pieces: I am about to rebuke your descendants, \q and I will smear dung on your faces, \q the dung of your festival sacrifices, \q and you will be carried off with it.

L.3: Look, I am rebuking your seed, \q and I will spread dung on your faces, \q the dung of your festival sacrifices; \q and you will be carried off to it.

R.3: I will punish your descendants. \q I will smear on your faces the dung from the animals you sacrifice at your festivals. \q Then you will be thrown out with it.

decisions.choice: rebuke your seed: punish your descendants
decisions.reason: "Seed" can mean crops or descendants. Since priests did not farm and the priesthood passed from father to son, the threat is probably against their descendants. With different vowels the word means "arm", and the Greek translation is generally said to read "I will cut off your arm", which would end their service at the altar.

decisions.choice: dung of your festival sacrifices: the waste from the sacrificed animals
decisions.reason: The dung and entrails of sacrificial animals were carried outside the camp and burned (Exodus 29:14; Leviticus 4:11-12; 16:27). The priests who handled the holy offerings will be smeared with the refuse and treated as refuse. |

decisions.choice: you will be carried off to it: thrown out with the refuse
decisions.reason: They will be taken away to the dung heap, unclean and removed from the LORD's service. |

decisions.choice: your seed (L), your descendants (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "seed", which can mean both; Balanced and Readable give the sense taken in m1. The word for "festivals" means the festival sacrifices, which Literal says too.

records.source: וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֚י שִׁלַּ֣חְתִּי אֲלֵיכֶ֔ם אֵ֖ת הַמִּצְוָ֣ה הַזֹּ֑את לִֽהְי֤וֹת בְּרִיתִי֙ אֶת־לֵוִ֔י אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And you will know that I have sent to you this commandment, [so that] my covenant with Levi may be, says Yahweh of hosts.
pieces: Then you will know that I have sent you this command \q so that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with Levi may stand, \q says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

L.4: And you will know that I have sent to you \q this commandment, \q that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant might be with Levi, \q says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.

R.4: Then you will know that I sent you this warning \q so that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with the tribe of Levi may continue, \q says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

decisions.choice: my covenant with Levi: the LORD's covenant with the priestly tribe
decisions.reason: Levi was the tribe from which the priests came. The LORD gave Levi charge of his teaching and his altar (Deuteronomy 33:8-11), and made a covenant of peace and of lasting priesthood with Phinehas, Aaron's grandson (Numbers 25:12-13). Jeremiah 33:21 and Nehemiah 13:29 also speak of the covenant with the Levites. |

decisions.choice: that my covenant might be with Levi: the warning was meant to keep the covenant
alternatives: so that my covenant with Levi might end
decisions.reason: The warning is given so that the covenant may continue, not be broken. Some take it the other way, as the end of the covenant, but verses 5-7 describe the covenant with approval.

decisions.choice: the tribe of Levi (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says that Levi stands for the tribe. |

records.source: בְּרִיתִ֣י׀הָיְתָ֣ה אִתּ֗וֹ הַֽחַיִּים֙ וְהַ֨שָּׁל֔וֹם וָאֶתְּנֵֽם־ל֥וֹ מוֹרָ֖א וַיִּֽירָאֵ֑נִי וּמִפְּנֵ֥י שְׁמִ֖י נִחַ֥ת הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: My covenant was with him, the life and the peace, and I gave them to him, fear; and he feared me, and before my name he was in awe.
pieces: My covenant with him was one of life and peace, \q and I gave them to him so that he would revere {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and he did revere {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} \q and stood in awe of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.

L.5: My covenant was with him, [a covenant] of life and peace, \q and I gave them to him [for] fear, and he feared {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \q and before {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name he stood in awe.

R.5: My covenant with Levi promised life and peace. \q I gave him these so that he would respect {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and he did respect {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q He was filled with awe before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: a covenant of life and peace
decisions.reason: The LORD gave Phinehas "my covenant of peace" (Numbers 25:12). Life and peace, full well-being, were what the covenant promised. |

decisions.choice: fear, awe: reverence that leads to obedience
decisions.reason: The LORD gave the covenant so that Levi would fear him, and Levi did. Fear here is the reverent awe of one who serves God faithfully (Deuteronomy 10:12). |

decisions.choice: life and peace; revere (B), respect (R)
decisions.reason: "Peace" follows the Isaiah table. Readable says "before me" for "before my name", since the name stands for the LORD himself. |

records.source: תּוֹרַ֤ת אֱמֶת֙ הָיְתָ֣ה בְּפִ֔יהוּ וְעַוְלָ֖ה לֹא־נִמְצָ֣א בִשְׂפָתָ֑יו בְּשָׁל֤וֹם וּבְמִישׁוֹר֙ הָלַ֣ךְ אִתִּ֔י וְרַבִּ֖ים הֵשִׁ֥יב מֵעָוֺֽן׃
records.gloss: Instruction of truth was in his mouth, and injustice was not found on his lips; in peace and in uprightness he walked with me, and many he turned back from iniquity.
pieces: True instruction was in his mouth, \q and nothing wrong was found on his lips. \q In peace and uprightness he walked with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q and he turned many back from sin.

L.6: True instruction was in his mouth, \q and no injustice was found on his lips; \q in peace and in uprightness he walked with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q and many he turned back from iniquity.

R.6: He taught what was true, \q and he never said anything wrong. \q He lived in peace with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and did what was right, \q and he helped many people turn away from sin.

decisions.choice: true instruction: reliable teaching of God's law
decisions.reason: Instruction (torah) is the priest's teaching of the LORD's ways (verse 7; Deuteronomy 33:10). "True" means faithful and reliable. |

decisions.choice: he walked with me: he lived in close fellowship with God
decisions.reason: Enoch and Noah "walked with God" (Genesis 5:22, 24; 6:9). The faithful priest lived near the LORD as well as serving him. |

decisions.choice: turned many back from iniquity: led many away from sin
decisions.reason: By teaching and example the faithful priest brought people back to the LORD. Daniel 12:3 speaks of those who lead many to righteousness. |

decisions.choice: instruction (L, B), taught (R); iniquity (L), sin (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Instruction" and "iniquity" follow the Isaiah table, with "teaching" and "sin" at Readable. |

records.source: כִּֽי־שִׂפְתֵ֤י כֹהֵן֙ יִשְׁמְרוּ־דַ֔עַת וְתוֹרָ֖ה יְבַקְשׁ֣וּ מִפִּ֑יהוּ כִּ֛י מַלְאַ֥ךְ יְהוָֽה־צְבָא֖וֹת הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: For [the] lips of a priest should guard knowledge, and instruction they should seek from his mouth, for [the] messenger of Yahweh of hosts [is] he.
pieces: For a priest's lips should preserve knowledge, \q and people should look to him for instruction, \q because he is the messenger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

L.7: For the lips of a priest should guard knowledge, \q and instruction they should seek from his mouth, \q for the messenger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts [is] he.

R.7: A priest should know God's teaching and keep it safe. \q People should be able to come to him to learn it, \q because he is the messenger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

decisions.choice: knowledge: the knowledge of God and his law
decisions.reason: Hosea 4:6 accuses the priests of rejecting knowledge, so that the people are destroyed for lack of it. The priest's lips are to keep that knowledge safe and pass it on. |

decisions.choice: the messenger of the LORD of hosts: the priest as one who carries God's word
decisions.reason: The word "messenger" is used of the prophet Haggai (Haggai 1:13), of the one the LORD will send (3:1), and in the prophet's own name, Malachi, "my messenger". Only here is a priest called the LORD's messenger: he speaks for God when he teaches. |

decisions.choice: messenger, lowercase at every level
decisions.reason: "Messenger" is lowercase, as in Haggai 1:13 and 3:1. Readable says "God's teaching" for knowledge and instruction together. |

records.source: וְאַתֶּם֙ סַרְתֶּ֣ם מִן־הַדֶּ֔רֶךְ הִכְשַׁלְתֶּ֥ם רַבִּ֖ים בַּתּוֹרָ֑ה שִֽׁחַתֶּם֙ בְּרִ֣ית הַלֵּוִ֔י אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: But you have turned aside from the way; you have caused many to stumble by the instruction; you have corrupted the covenant of Levi, says Yahweh of hosts.
pieces: But you have turned from the way \q and caused many to stumble by your instruction. \q You have ruined the covenant of Levi, \q says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

L.8: But you have turned aside from the way; \q you have made many stumble by [your] instruction; \q you have corrupted the covenant of Levi, \q says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.

R.8: But you priests have stopped living the way you should. \q Your teaching has led many people into sin. \q You have broken the covenant I made with Levi, \q says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

decisions.choice: turned aside from the way: left the path the LORD set
decisions.reason: The same words describe Israel's turning to the golden calf (Exodus 32:8; Deuteronomy 9:12). The priests do the opposite of Levi, who turned many back (verse 6). |

decisions.choice: by your instruction: by the way you teach the law
decisions.reason: The word can mean "in the law" or "by the instruction". Their teaching, which should keep people from falling, makes them stumble.

decisions.choice: corrupted: ruined, spoiled
decisions.reason: The verb is from the same root as the "blemished" animal of 1:14. The priests who offer spoiled animals have spoiled the covenant. |

decisions.choice: stopped living the way you should (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what turning from the way means. |

records.source: וְגַם־אֲנִ֞י נָתַ֧תִּי אֶתְכֶ֛ם נִבְזִ֥ים וּשְׁפָלִ֖ים לְכָל־הָעָ֑ם כְּפִ֗י אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֵֽינְכֶם֙ שֹׁמְרִ֣ים אֶת־דְּרָכַ֔י וְנֹשְׂאִ֥ים פָּנִ֖ים בַּתּוֹרָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And I also have made you despised and low to all the people, according as you are not keeping my ways and are lifting up faces in the instruction.
pieces: So I in turn have made you contemptible and lowly in the eyes of all the people, \q since you have not kept to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} ways \q and you show favoritism in your instruction.

L.9: So I in turn have made you despised and low before all the people, \q because you are not keeping {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} ways \q but are showing partiality in [your] instruction.

R.9: So I have made all the people look down on you and think you are worthless. \q This is because you have not obeyed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q When you teach the law, you favor some people over others.

decisions.choice: lifting up faces: showing favor, partiality
decisions.reason: To "lift up the face" of someone is to favor them. In the law it is forbidden to judges (Leviticus 19:15; Deuteronomy 10:17). The priests hoped that God would lift up their faces (1:8-9), but they show favor to the powerful in their own rulings. |

decisions.choice: I also have made you despised: the punishment answers the sin
decisions.reason: The priests despised the LORD's name (1:6); he makes them despised before the people. |

decisions.choice: obeyed me (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "obeyed me" for "kept my ways". |

records.source: הֲל֨וֹא אָ֤ב אֶחָד֙ לְכֻלָּ֔נוּ הֲל֛וֹא אֵ֥ל אֶֽחָ֖ד בְּרָאָ֑נוּ מַדּ֗וּעַ נִבְגַּד֙ אִ֣ישׁ בְּאָחִ֔יו לְחַלֵּ֖ל בְּרִ֥ית אֲבֹתֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: [Is there] not one father for all of us? Did not one God create us? Why do we act faithlessly, each against his brother, to profane [the] covenant of our fathers?
pieces: Do we not all have one father? \q Was it not one God who created us? \q So why are we unfaithful to one another, \q profaning the covenant of our ancestors?

L.10: Is there not one father for all of us? \q Did not one God create us? \q Why do we act faithlessly, each against {{gender:another|his brother}}, \q profaning the covenant of our fathers?

R.10: We all have the same father, do we not? \q The same God created all of us. \q So why are we unfaithful to one another? \q Why do we break the covenant God made with our ancestors?

decisions.choice: one father: God, the father of his people
alternatives: Abraham or Jacob, the father of the nation
decisions.reason: The next line, "one God created us", suggests that the father is God, as in 1:6 and Isaiah 63:16; 64:7. Some think of Abraham (Isaiah 51:2) or of Jacob. Either way the people are one family.

decisions.choice: act faithlessly: break faith, betray
decisions.reason: The verb means to betray a trust, to be unfaithful in a relationship. It is the key word of 2:10-16, where it is used five times, of betrayal of one another, of God, and of one's wife. |

decisions.choice: we, us: the prophet speaks as one of the people
decisions.reason: A new dispute begins (2:10-16), about faithlessness in the community and in marriage. The prophet includes himself with those he speaks to. |

decisions.choice: each against another (L, gender default), one another (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Brother" here means a fellow member of the people, men and women, so Literal uses the gender setting; Balanced and Readable say "one another". |

records.heading: Unfaithful to one another

records.source: בָּגְדָ֣ה יְהוּדָ֔ה וְתוֹעֵבָ֛ה נֶעֶשְׂתָ֥ה בְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וּבִירֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כִּ֣י׀חִלֵּ֣ל יְהוּדָ֗ה קֹ֤דֶשׁ יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָהֵ֔ב וּבָעַ֖ל בַּת־אֵ֥ל נֵכָֽר׃
records.gloss: Judah has acted faithlessly, and an abomination has been done in Israel and in Jerusalem; for Judah has profaned the holiness of Yahweh, which he loves, and has married [the] daughter of a foreign god.
pieces: Judah has been unfaithful, \q and a detestable practice has been carried out in Israel and in Jerusalem. \q Judah has profaned what is holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loves, \q by marrying the daughter of a foreign god.

L.11: Judah has acted faithlessly, \q and an abomination has been done in Israel and in Jerusalem; \q for Judah has profaned what is holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loves, \q and has married a daughter of a foreign god.

R.11: The people of Judah have been unfaithful. \q They have done a disgusting thing in Israel and in Jerusalem. \q They have treated as common the things that are holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loves. \q The men have married women who worship a foreign god.

decisions.choice: married the daughter of a foreign god: married women who worshiped other gods
decisions.reason: A "daughter" of a god is a woman who belongs to it as a worshiper (compare Numbers 21:29, the "sons and daughters" of Chemosh). The law forbade marriage with the peoples of Canaan because they would lead Israel to other gods (Deuteronomy 7:3-4). Ezra and Nehemiah faced the same problem in their day (Ezra 9:1-2; Nehemiah 13:23-27). The issue is the worship of other gods, not race. |

decisions.choice: what is holy to the LORD, which he loves: the holy people, or the temple
decisions.reason: The word means "holiness, what is holy". It may be the temple, which the LORD loves (Psalm 78:68), or the people themselves, set apart as holy to him (Jeremiah 2:3; Ezra 9:2, "the holy seed"). The wording keeps both possible.

decisions.choice: an abomination: something detestable to the LORD
decisions.reason: The word is used of practices the LORD hates, especially the worship of other gods (Deuteronomy 7:25-26; 12:31). |

decisions.choice: abomination (L), detestable practice (B), disgusting thing (R)
decisions.reason: The word follows the table set for Ezekiel. Readable says that the men married, which the verse implies, and says "women who worship a foreign god" for "the daughter of a foreign god". |

records.source: יַכְרֵ֨ת יְהוָ֜ה לָאִ֨ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר יַעֲשֶׂ֨נָּה֙ עֵ֣ר וְעֹנֶ֔ה מֵאָהֳלֵ֖י יַֽעֲקֹ֑ב וּמַגִּ֣ישׁ מִנְחָ֔ה לַֽיהוָ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃פ
records.gloss: May Yahweh cut off the man who does it, one who wakes and one who answers, from [the] tents of Jacob, and one who brings an offering to Yahweh of hosts.
pieces: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} cut off from the tents of Jacob \q every man who does this, whoever he may be, \q even if he brings an offering \q to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

L.12: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} cut off the man who does this, one who wakes and one who answers, \q from the tents of Jacob, \q even one who brings an offering \q to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.

R.12: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} remove from the people of Israel every man who does this, no matter who he is, \q even if he brings offerings \q to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

decisions.choice: one who wakes and one who answers: anyone at all
decisions.reason: The phrase is obscure. It seems to pair two kinds of person to mean "everyone", as "the watchman and the one who answers him", "teacher and pupil" or "the one who calls and the one who answers". Some read it of the man's descendants: he will have no one left in Israel.

decisions.choice: the tents of Jacob: the people of Israel
decisions.reason: "Tents" stand for homes and families, a memory of the people's early life (Numbers 24:5; Jeremiah 30:18). To be cut off from them is to lose one's place among God's people. |

decisions.choice: even one who brings an offering: worship does not cover the sin
decisions.reason: Bringing offerings to the LORD does not protect a man who has broken faith in this way. Verse 13 says why his offerings are refused. |

decisions.choice: whoever he may be (B), no matter who he is (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the obscure pair (m1). The man is a husband, so no gender setting is used. Readable says "the people of Israel" for "the tents of Jacob".

records.source: וְזֹאת֙ שֵׁנִ֣ית תַּֽעֲשׂ֔וּ כַּסּ֤וֹת דִּמְעָה֙ אֶת־מִזְבַּ֣ח יְהוָ֔ה בְּכִ֖י וַֽאֲנָקָ֑ה מֵאֵ֣ין ע֗וֹד פְּנוֹת֙ אֶל־הַמִּנְחָ֔ה וְלָקַ֥חַת רָצ֖וֹן מִיֶּדְכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And this second [thing] you do: covering the altar of Yahweh [with] tears, weeping and groaning, because there is no longer turning to the offering or taking [it with] favor from your hand.
pieces: And here is another thing you do: \q you flood {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s altar with tears, \q weeping and groaning, \q because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} no longer looks on your offerings \q or accepts them gladly from your hands.

L.13: And this second thing you do: \q covering the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with tears, \q weeping and groaning, \q because there is no longer [any] turning to the offering \q or taking [it with] favor from your hand.

R.13: Here is another thing you do. \q You cry and moan and make {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s altar wet with your tears, \q because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} no longer pays attention to your offerings \q or accepts them from you with pleasure.

decisions.choice: this second thing: a further charge
decisions.reason: The prophet adds a second charge to that of verses 11-12, or turns to a second wrong: their unfaithfulness to their own wives (verse 14). |

decisions.choice: covering the altar with tears: weeping in worship because the LORD refuses the offerings
alternatives: the tears of wives sent away
decisions.reason: The worshipers weep and groan at the altar because their offerings are no longer accepted, and in verse 14 they ask why. Some think of the tears of the wives they have divorced, which reach God's altar, but the verse links the tears to the refused offerings.

decisions.choice: your offerings (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "your offerings", which the end of the verse ("from your hand") implies. |

records.heading: The wife of your youth

records.source: וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֖ם עַל־מָ֑ה עַ֡ל כִּי־יְהוָה֩ הֵעִ֨יד בֵּינְךָ֜ וּבֵ֣ין׀אֵ֣שֶׁת נְעוּרֶ֗יךָ אֲשֶׁ֤ר אַתָּה֙ בָּגַ֣דְתָּה בָּ֔הּ וְהִ֥יא חֲבֶרְתְּךָ֖ וְאֵ֥שֶׁת בְּרִיתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And you say, Because of what? Because Yahweh has been witness between you and between [the] wife of your youth, with whom you have dealt faithlessly, though she [is] your companion and [the] wife of your covenant.
pieces: Yet you ask, "Why?" \q Because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was a witness between you and the wife you married in your youth. You have broken faith with her, \q though she is your partner and your wife by covenant.

L.14: But you say, "Why?" \q Because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has testified between you and the wife of your youth, with whom you have dealt faithlessly, \q though she is your companion and the wife of your covenant.

R.14: You ask, "Why?" \q It is because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was a witness when you married your wife when you were young. You have broken faith with her, \q though she is your partner, the wife you made a covenant with.

decisions.choice: the LORD a witness: marriage is a covenant made before God
decisions.reason: Marriage is called a covenant, with God as witness (Proverbs 2:17; compare Genesis 31:50). To betray one's wife is to break a covenant God witnessed, and so to wrong God himself. |

decisions.choice: the wife of your youth: the wife a man married when young
decisions.reason: The phrase speaks of the first love and long years shared (Proverbs 5:18; Isaiah 54:6). Men were apparently divorcing these wives, perhaps to marry the foreign women of verse 11. |

decisions.choice: your companion: your partner
decisions.reason: The word means a close companion, one joined to another. It is found only here of a wife. |

decisions.choice: "Why?" (all levels)
decisions.reason: The people's question is set in double quotes, as in every dispute of the book. |

records.source: וְלֹא־אֶחָ֣ד עָשָׂ֗ה וּשְׁאָ֥ר ר֨וּחַ֙ ל֔וֹ וּמָה֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ד מְבַקֵּ֖שׁ זֶ֣רַע אֱלֹהִ֑ים וְנִשְׁמַרְתֶּם֙ בְּר֣וּחֲכֶ֔ם וּבְאֵ֥שֶׁת נְעוּרֶ֖יךָ אַל־יִבְגֹּֽד׃
records.gloss: And not one has made, and a remnant of spirit [belongs] to him? And what [is] the one? Seeking offspring of God. So guard yourselves in your spirit, and against [the] wife of your youth let none act faithlessly.
pieces: Did {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not make them one, with a portion of spirit in their union? \q And why one? \q Because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was seeking godly offspring. \q So guard yourselves in your spirit, \q and let no one be unfaithful to the wife of his youth.

L.15: And did not one make [them], with a remnant of spirit [belonging] to it? \q And what does the one seek? \q Offspring of God. \q So take heed to your spirit, \q and against the wife of your youth let no one act faithlessly.

R.15: Did not God make husband and wife one, in body and spirit? \q Why did {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} make them one? \q Because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wanted children who would belong to God. \q So be careful, \q and do not be unfaithful to the wife you married when you were young.

decisions.choice: did he not make them one, with a portion of spirit in their union? ... seeking godly offspring
alternatives: no one who has a remnant of the spirit would do this
did not the one God make us, and preserve our life?
decisions.reason: The first half of the verse is among the hardest in the prophets, and the ancient translations already differ. The reading taken here, that God made husband and wife one, recalls Genesis 2:24 ("they become one flesh"), and gives a reason for faithfulness: God seeks offspring who belong to him. Other readings take "one" as God, or say that no one with even a little of the spirit would act so, and "the one" as Abraham, who sought offspring by taking Hagar.

decisions.choice: offspring of God: godly children
decisions.reason: "Offspring of God" means children who belong to God and are raised in faithfulness to him (compare Ezra 9:2, "the holy seed"). |

decisions.choice: take heed to your spirit: watch yourselves, keep your heart
decisions.reason: The words mean to take great care, to watch over one's inner life (Deuteronomy 4:9, 15). They are repeated in verse 16. |

decisions.choice: [them] (L), them (B), husband and wife (R)
decisions.reason: Each level supplies the object of "make", following m1; Literal brackets it. Balanced and Readable name God as the subject, which the verse implies; Readable says "in body and spirit" to give "a portion of spirit" a sense a young reader can follow.

records.source: כִּֽי־שָׂנֵ֣א שַׁלַּ֗ח אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְכִסָּ֤ה חָמָס֙ עַל־לְבוּשׁ֔וֹ אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת וְנִשְׁמַרְתֶּ֥ם בְּרוּחֲכֶ֖ם וְלֹ֥א תִבְגֹּֽדוּ׃ס
records.gloss: For [he] hates sending away, says Yahweh, the God of Israel, and covering violence over his garment, says Yahweh of hosts. So guard yourselves in your spirit, and do not act faithlessly.
pieces: For I hate divorce, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, \q and I hate it when a man covers his garment with violence, \q says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. \q So guard yourselves in your spirit, and do not be unfaithful.

L.16: For [he] hates divorce, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, \q and [one who] covers violence over his garment, \q says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts. \q So take heed to your spirit, and do not act faithlessly.

R.16: I hate divorce, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel. \q I hate it when a man stains himself with violence, \q says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. \q So be careful, and do not be unfaithful.

decisions.choice: For he hates divorce, says the LORD: the LORD hates divorce
alternatives: the man who hates and divorces covers his garment with violence
if you hate her, send her away
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is hard. Read as here, "he hates" has the LORD as its subject, as the words "says the LORD" suggest, and the LORD declares that he hates divorce and the violence done with it. The main other reading takes the man as the subject of both verbs: "the one who hates and divorces covers his garment with violence", that is, a man who divorces his wife out of dislike does her violence. The Greek translation and one of the Qumran scrolls are generally said to read "if you hate her, send her away", which would permit divorce and goes against the rest of the passage. All the readings agree that the LORD condemns the treachery of verses 14-15.

decisions.choice: covers his garment with violence: violence clings to him like a stain on his clothes
alternatives: wrongs the wife he took under his garment
decisions.reason: Wrongdoing worn like clothing is a common picture (Psalm 73:6; 109:18). A man spread his garment over a woman as a sign of marriage (Ruth 3:9; Ezekiel 16:8), so some read "garment" as the wife herself, wronged by her husband.

decisions.choice: divorce: sending a wife away
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for divorce in Deuteronomy 24:1-4: a man "sends her out of his house". |

decisions.choice: I hate (B, R); [he] hates (L)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "he hates" within words the LORD speaks. Literal keeps the third person with brackets, as set for this verse; Balanced and Readable say "I hate", because the LORD is the speaker (m1). Readable says "stains himself with violence" for "covers his garment with violence", the first sense in m2.

records.source: הוֹגַעְתֶּ֤ם יְהוָה֙ בְּדִבְרֵיכֶ֔ם וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֖ם בַּמָּ֣ה הוֹגָ֑עְנוּ בֶּאֱמָרְכֶ֗ם כָּל־עֹ֨שֵׂה רָ֜ע ט֣וֹב׀בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֗ה וּבָהֶם֙ ה֣וּא חָפֵ֔ץ א֥וֹ אַיֵּ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י הַמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃
records.gloss: You have wearied Yahweh with your words. And you say, In what have we wearied [him]? In your saying, Everyone who does evil [is] good in [the] eyes of Yahweh, and in them he delights; or, Where [is] the God of justice?
pieces: You have wearied {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with your words. \q Yet you ask, "In what way have we wearied {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?" \q When you say, "All who do evil are good in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s sight, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is pleased with them," \q or by asking, "Where is the God of justice?"

L.17: You have wearied {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with your words. \q But you say, "How have we wearied {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?" \q By your saying, "Everyone who does evil is good in the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} delights in them," \q or else, "Where is the God of justice?"

R.17: You have made {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} tired of listening to you. \q But you ask, "How have we made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} tired?" \q You say, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} thinks that everyone who does evil is good, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is happy with them." \q Or you ask, "Where is the God who judges fairly?"

decisions.choice: you have wearied the LORD: you have tried his patience
decisions.reason: Isaiah 43:24 has the LORD say, "you have wearied me with your iniquities". Here it is their words that weary him. |

decisions.choice: "Where is the God of justice?": the people doubt that God judges
decisions.reason: The people see the wicked prosper and conclude that God approves of them, or that he does not care. The dispute runs on into 3:1-5, where the LORD answers: he will come to his temple to judge. |

decisions.choice: the God of justice: the God who judges rightly
decisions.reason: "The LORD is a God of justice" (Isaiah 30:18). |

decisions.choice: wearied him; delights in them (L), pleased (B), happy (R)
decisions.reason: The people's words are in double quotes, and their pronouns for God take the deity_pronoun setting. Readable says "made the LORD tired of listening" for "wearied the LORD with your words". |
